artworks.title: Fulmer Petrel
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is a painting of a Fulmar Petrel standing on a rock against a seascape background. The bird is depicted in meticulous detail, sitting upright with its yellow-grey plumage and white head. It stands atop a rounded rock, its webbed feet prominently visible in the foreground. The background shows a body of water extending to the horizon with a cloudy sky.

artworks.title: Buff-breasted Sandpiper
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is a painting of two buff-breasted sandpipers on a rocky shore by a body of water. The painting depicts two birds in different poses; one stands upright on the rocky ground, while the other is lowering its body with wings slightly spread. The birds have a prominent buff color on their breasts and intricate patterns on their wings and back. The background features water reflecting land with distant hills visible, under a clear sky.

artworks.title: Common Cormorant
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is a painting of three cormorants near a rocky shoreline. The painting features two adult cormorants and two chicks. One adult is seen crouched over a nest containing the two chicks, perched securely on a rocky ledge amongst dried twigs and foliage, while the other adult stands nearby with its beak open. The feathers of the cormorants are depicted with impressive detail, showcasing a variety of textures and colors. The background consists of rocky cliffs under a blue sky with soft clouds. The style of the painting suggests it is in the style of John James Audubon.

artworks.title: Arctic Jager
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is a painting of two birds in a coastal landscape. One bird is perched on a rocky cliff, while the other is depicted in flight above it. The birds have sleek black heads and elongated tail feathers. The background includes a calm sea with a distant view of rugged cliffs and a few scattered clouds in a pale blue sky. The painting details the plumage of the birds with great precision, highlighting the texture and coloration of their feathers. The scene captures a sense of natural serenity and the majesty of the birds' environment.

artworks.title: American Woodcock
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is a painting of American Woodcocks in a natural setting. Three birds are depicted amidst tall green grass. Their long, slender beaks are pointed towards the ground. The composition captures the intricate feather patterns and the interaction between the birds and their environment.

artworks.title: Greenshank
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is a painting of a Greenshank standing on the edge of a fortification with a coastal scene in the background. The bird is depicted with a long, slender neck and legs, looking towards the distance. Its feathers show intricate patterns in shades of brown and white, and its beak is long and pointed. The landscape behind the bird features a fort with a canon, leading to a stretch of water, with a distant view of a town along the coastline under a partly cloudy sky. The style is reminiscent of John James Audubon.

artworks.title: Stormy Petrel
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is a painting of two stormy petrels flying over ocean waves. One bird is shown in profile with wings spread, while the other is seen from the back. A small barrel floats in the water below them. The style is reminiscent of John James Audubon's detailed bird illustrations.

artworks.title: Frigate Pelican
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is a painting of a frigate bird in flight. The painting shows a large, dark frigate bird with outstretched wings, set against a plain background. The bird is depicted in a dynamic position, giving a sense of movement as if it is gliding through the air. Its elongated wings and forked tail are detailed with precise, layered feathers that range from a deep-black to hints of iridescent hues. The bird's beak is pointed and open, and its eye is visible. Above the bird, two small depictions of feet are visible.

artworks.title: Richardson's Jager
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: The image shows two large birds. One bird is standing on the ground on the left, while the other is perched on a rock on the right. Both birds have feathers in earthy tones such as browns, blacks, and whites, with some blue-gray on their legs and beaks. The bird on the left is facing slightly to the right, and the bird on the right is standing on the rock, suggesting an upward perspective. The background displays a muted, cloudy sky with subtle landscapes.

artworks.title: Cayenne Tern
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is a painting of a Cayenne Tern standing on a rocky shore with a crab nearby, done in the style of John James Audubon. The image features a large bird, known as a Cayenne Tern, poised on the edge of a shoreline. The tern has white feathers and a distinctive black head with a red-orange beak. Perched on its legs, the bird's feet are on the ground. Below, a red crab is visible, with its claws out. The background shows gray-blue skies and dark waters, indicating an overcast day. Rocks surround the setting, illustrating the natural coastal habitat. The painting is detailed, capturing the patterns of the bird's feathers and the texture of the crab's shell.

artworks.title: Semi-palmated Snipe or Willet
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is a painting of shorebirds among grassy terrain and rocks. The image features three birds with detailed features like elongated legs and pointed beaks. Two birds are on the ground with pale blue legs and grayish-brown plumage patterns. The third bird is in a dynamic pose, slightly bent with wings partly open. Lush green grasses and rocks surround the birds in the painting.

artworks.title: Noddy Tern
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is a painting of a Noddy Tern perched on a branch by the water. The illustration features a detailed depiction of the bird with its sleek plumage in various shades of brown and a distinctive white cap on its head. The bird stands on a rugged, textured branch that extends diagonally. The background showcases a coastal landscape with calm waters and distant landforms, likely cliffs or hills, under a soft, muted sky. Detail is also given to the texture and feather patterns of the tern. This is in the style of John James Audubon.

artworks.title: King Duck
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This image depicts two ducks by a rocky shoreline. The duck on the left has a white body with black wings, a greenish-blue head, and a pinkish beak, standing on a rock. The duck on the right is brown with detailed feathers, sitting on the ground. The background shows an ocean with distant hills or cliffs. The painting demonstrates a high level of detail, capturing the textures of the feathers and rocks. This artwork is inspired by the style of John James Audubon.

artworks.title: Hutchin's Barnacle Goose
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is a painting of a Canada Goose standing on a rock by the water, with snowy mountains in the background. The painting features a solitary Canada Goose, standing on a rocky outcropping next to a body of water. The background shows distant, snow-capped mountains under a cloudy sky. The goose is depicted in a detailed and realistic manner, with a black head and neck, a white chinstrap, and brown plumage with lighter feather edges. The style is similar to that of John James Audubon. The goose is positioned with its head raised.

artworks.title: Schinz's Sandpiper
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: The image shows a coastal scene with a sandy shore and the sea. A bird is in flight on the left, with its wings spread, while another bird stands on the sand. The horizon is visible with a distant strip of land, palm trees, and hills. The artwork features detailed rendering of the birds and shells on the sand, using earth tones and muted blues for the water.

artworks.title: Sandwich Tern
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is a painting of a Sandwich Tern on a rocky surface near a body of water with a lobster nearby. The Sandwich Tern is perched on a rocky outcrop with one leg raised. Its plumage is light gray and white with black on its head and a yellow tip on its beak. The background is a blue-toned seascape. Next to the bird is a detailed depiction of a lobster. This painting is in the style of John James Audubon.

artworks.title: Black Tern
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: The image shows two black terns. The larger bird stands on a rock, while the other is flying. The standing bird is positioned near the bottom center of the image on a light brown rock against a serene background of calm blue water and a distant landscape. The sky is light blue with subtle white clouds. The flying bird dives downwards from the upper left towards the bottom right, displaying its pale gray underbelly and black-tipped wings. The colors in the image include shades of black, gray, blue, and brown.

artworks.title: Great White Heron
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is a painting of a Great White Heron catching a fish. The scene shows the heron with detailed white and grey feathers, holding a pink and yellow-striped fish with its long beak. The heron stands on yellow and green legs with a backdrop of a calm sea, distant shoreline, and faintly-sketched buildings. The sky is blue with darker clouds, creating depth and atmosphere. The painting is in the style of John James Audubon.

artworks.title: White-winged Silvery Gull
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is a painting of two large gulls perched on a rocky landscape. The white-winged silvery gulls are depicted with one bird resting on the ground and the other balancing on the edge of a rocky outcrop above. The seabirds are intricately detailed with fine feather markings and distinct color gradations from pale cream to soft gray. The background includes rocky cliffs and an overcast sky. The painting is in the style of John James Audubon, known for detailed and realistic bird paintings.

artworks.title: Wandering Shearwater
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is a painting of a bird named the Wandering Shearwater. The bird is shown standing on a rocky surface with a calm body of water and silhouetted mountains in the background. The bird has white underparts and darker plumage on the wings and back. Its beak is slightly open, with a unique curve and coloration matching its feet. The painting highlights the bird's plumage pattern, with a naturalistic setting enhancing its presentation. The style is reminiscent of John James Audubon's detailed and vibrant bird illustrations.

artworks.title: Purple Sandpiper
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is a painting of three Purple Sandpipers on rocky terrain near a body of water. The left bird has brown and white plumage, walking along a flat rocky surface. The two birds on the right have darker, purple-tinged feathers and are positioned stepping down from a rock. The background shows a subtle gradient suggesting a sky and a horizon line indicating water. The style is similar to the work of John James Audubon, known for detailed studies of American birds in their natural habitats.

artworks.title: Fork-tailed Gull
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is a painting of two birds near a body of water. The scene depicts a large bird standing atop a rock with a smaller bird to its left. The larger bird has grey and white plumage with a black ring around its neck and a yellow-tipped black beak. The smaller bird is pecking or foraging with its beak on the sandy ground. Seashells are visible on the ground. The background shows tranquil water, a distant shoreline, and a sky with soft clouds. The style is similar to that of John James Audubon.

artworks.title: White-fronted Goose
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is a painting featuring two white-fronted geese. The image shows two geese against a backdrop of tall green grasses. One goose is upright with its head turned, displaying its coloration and feather details. The other goose has its head raised and wings partially spread. Both birds have warm brown tones on their heads and necks, contrasting with whites and grays on their bodies. The painting captures the textures of their plumage and the colors of their beaks and feet. Shells and rocks are also seen beneath the geese.

artworks.title: Ivory Gull
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: The image features two ivory gulls. One gull is on the left, perched atop moss-covered ground, while the other gull is on the right, standing on a rocky surface. The gulls have white plumage with gray markings, dark legs, and faintly yellow bills. The color palette includes blues, grays, and earthy tones. In the foreground, small shells and stones are scattered near the base of each gull.
